redaction_note: Redacted 2026-08-09, twice. As written on 2026-08-06 every row carried learner_sentence / expected / predicted / the baseline's own correction, so the four items this run got wrong could be read straight out of the file — inside the repository whose design.md says they are not written down (docs/ja/glossary.md §7). The first redaction kept the format columns and did NOT close the leak: `japanese_left_unquoted` is only ever set when the model returned a reason, so it means `predicted: true`, and joined against the published `needs_correction` labels it named the same four items again. A `test` run now writes no per-item rows at all. The aggregate numbers above are unchanged and were not recomputed. The unredacted version stays in git history at commit a27ad4a: it cannot be removed without rewriting a published history, so it is named here instead of quietly dropped.
items_note: Backfilled 2026-08-12. This run was measured against the 60-item file at commit 7857c94 (dev 40 / test 20); the current items.json holds 120 and its test split is 40, so the two are not the same measurement. The digest is the one that was in force at the time, not today's — writing today's would put a value in the field whose whole job is to say which data a number came from.
thresholds_note: Backfilled 2026-08-12, and RECONSTRUCTED rather than observed. The field was added after these runs, so the value is the digest of config/thresholds.toml at the nearest commit that could have been in the working tree at the time — a27ad4a for the correction runs, e7a0735 for the compliance ones. Both commits landed minutes AFTER the runs they are attributed to (18 and 3-7 minutes), so an edit in between would not show. Recorded this way because today's digest would be plainly wrong, and a blank field would lose the only evidence there is. Runs from 2026-08-12 onward carry the digest observed at run time.
